newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli unlinked bonds end higher.
newsitem.headline: Israeli unlinked bonds end higher.

text.p: Unlinked bonds led a generally higher Israeli bond market on Monday, but dollar-linked bonds fell, traders said.
* Unlinked government bonds (Gilon - issued for four years): +0.13 pct to 169.67.
* Bank of Israel short-term Makam bills: +0.06 pct to 160.46
Volume was low at 147 million shekels with most of the activity concentrated in inflation-linked bonds, traders said.
"Activity in CPI-linked bonds was mixed with a moderate rise in the long bonds and a mild decline in the short bonds," said Uri Schur of Eyal Securities.

Yields on inflation-linked long bonds have fallen sharply over the previous two months to 4.44 percent from 5.2 percent. But Gidi Halperin at Meitav Investments and Securities said the trend would not continue much longer because yields on unlinked bonds now reflect inflationary expectations of 10.3 percent over the next 12 months.
"The only reason that long bonds are still rising is that the (provident) funds are trying to show improved returns for the end of the year," he said
Schur agreed, saying: "Yields on unlinked bonds have fallen sharply recently and we expect that prices will not rise any further in the near future," he said.

Prices for unlinked bonds have also reached a ceiling, Schur said. "Demand for the Makams is falling. The market has reached the saturation point. Yields fell today from 15.2 percent to 14.8 percent, although they will not decline much further," he predicted.
Traders noted that total volume in the Makams was a low 28 million shekels.

Dollar-linked bonds declined as the shekel continued to rise against the dollar. In the local foreign currency market, the representative rate for the dollar was fixed at 3.2270 shekels against 3.2350 on Friday.
Note: Makams are zero-coupon unlinked certificates with durations of three months to one year. The Bank of Israel issues Makams to absorb liquidity.
